findings.claim: OBL-1's reason still denies the exact claim v4 exists to make, because the sentence was carried over from v3 unchanged.
findings.evidence: I diffed every obligation reason against live v3. Six of seven are byte-identical to v3 and only OBL-2's was rewritten. OBL-1's carried-over text ends: 'This join does not retarget those namings. It does not claim OBL-2 harness specifications are authored.' In v3 that sentence was true and consistent - v3 held harnessSpecificationsNotAuthored true and its OBL-2 reason said the five identifiers were 'named and not authored'. v4 reverses that position but leaves the sentence in place, so the file now asserts and denies the same proposition. The denial is not local to OBL-1: the subject of the sentence is 'This join'.
findings.whyItMatters: This is the one claim v4 exists to land. Its own purpose field says 'v4 lands the stale "specifications not authored" claim', and the stale claim lived in two places - summary and OBL-1's prose. v4 landed it in summary and OBL-2 and missed OBL-1, so the landing is incomplete in the artifact whose sole novelty is that landing. A coordinator auditing whether v4 measures the specifications as authored gets opposite answers from the same file depending on which field is read.
findings.notAReadingProblem: I looked for a reading that saves the sentence and did not find one. Construing 'It' as OBL-1 rather than the join makes the sentence vacuous rather than true. Construing 'does not claim they are authored' as 'does not itself author them' would make it true, but that is a different proposition and the subject already states it separately and correctly at doesNot 'Does not invent G01-G05 harness specifications.' The verb here is claim, not author.
findings.remedyOptionSpace: Either drop the sentence from OBL-1, or restate it to the residual proposition that survives the reversal - that the join does not itself author the specifications and does not retarget the G01-G05 namings. I am naming the option space only. I am not authoring replacement bytes, and I record here that if a successor reproduces any wording of mine verbatim, that exactness is my own text returning and is not independent corroboration.
findings.severityReasoning: Not a blocker and not a must-fix. Every operative field is correct and independently verified: OBL-1's own disposition of leftoverDesign false and capable-of-riding stands on v16 specifying threeCores, defaultInstall and inventorySchema, and does not depend on the false sentence; the summary lists, ride standings, gate owners, flags and denials are all sound. Nothing a coordinator would record from this file is wrong. The defect is a false statement in prose that contradicts the file's central claim, which under the standard I have applied to this class - stated rule false, operative result correct - is a SHOULD-FIX.

observationsNotFindings: The v3-to-v4 delta is unusually tight and that is to the artifact's credit. Exactly one summary flag flips, one flag is added, one obligation reason is rewritten, and six obligation reasons are byte-identical to v3. A join that had quietly rewritten several reasons while flipping a flag would have been much harder to audit. The single defect is on the other side of that same discipline - a reason that should have changed did not.

v3's OBL-2 reason set an explicit release condition: 'OBL-2 stays leftover-design until independently reviewed G01-G05 harness specifications exist.' Those specifications now exist, so a reader applying v3's condition literally would expect OBL-2 to flip to leftoverDesign false. v4 keeps it true on a second limb - the D-006 unit and G02 tree-accounting - that v3's sentence did not mention. I checked whether this was goalpost-moving and concluded it is not: live G02 bytes independently establish that limb, so the residue is real and predates v4. It is worth the coordinator noting that v3's release condition was necessary but not sufficient, which v3's own wording did not convey.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: REJECT on one SHOULD-FIX; no blockers, no must-fix. v4's substance holds. OBL-2 stays open on a limb I verified independently: live G02 bytes say size comparison to 80 MB is scored only after a D-006 unit-and-accounting successor, no such successor exists, and the subject invents no unit - zero occurrences of MB, MiB or any unit token. The defect is narrow and structural. Six of seven obligation reasons are byte-identical to v3 and only OBL-2's was rewritten; OBL-1's carried-over reason still ends 'This join does not retarget those namings. It does not claim OBL-2 harness specifications are authored', where 'It' is 'This join'. The stale claim lived in two places and v4 landed it in one, so the artifact whose sole purpose is landing that claim did not finish landing it.
